projects.title_en: InEU - Inventer l'Europe
projects.action_type: Jean Monnet Actions in Other Fields of Education and Training - Learning EU initiatives
projects.objective: Our project aims to make 4th grade students think about both the modern idea of ​​Europe and the origins of the EU. For this objective, we cannot avoid a return to the 18th century. Indeed, whether the founding fathers of the Union - Jean Monnet, Robert Schuman, all those whom the British historian Alan Milward called the "European saints" - or its architects, all summoned Montesquieu and Voltaire as a source of 'inspiration. So to use the words of Tzvetan Todorov in his essay The Spirit of Enlightenment (2006) “Without Europe, no Enlightenment, without the Enlightenment, no Europe”? The Enlightenment thinks and says Europe. The Age of Enlightenment gave rise to a European art of living and a feeling of belonging to the same culture. With the ideas of the great philosophers mixed with the circulation of fashions and witticisms, as well as the travels of enlightened men, the Enlightenment is a prestigious creation of Europe. Thinking about the Europe of this century means giving students a glimpse of questions that are still relevant today, which are those of European identity as a breeding ground for possible European citizenship, as a first step towards political unity. projects.objective:
The Madeleine Vionnet High School is a vocational secondary school located in Bondy. It offers a diverse range of training programs in Fashion Professions, Administrative Management, and Personal Care Services. The school also includes two classes of Higher National Diploma (BTS) in Fashion Professions - Garments, a Complementary Local Initiative Training (FCIL), and a CAP Early Childhood training program in partnership with GRETA.
Since September 2022, the school has opened a European section class in English within the Fashion Professions - Garments program, providing students with enhanced language training and cultural enrichment. Currently, the European second-year class consists of 14 students, while the first-year class has 24 students. The school serves a total of 405 secondary students and 53 higher education students, with most young women (85% of the total student body). More than half of the students (208) receive financial aid, reflecting a socio-economic context that requires particular support to ensure their success and broaden their horizons.

projects.title_en: AVENIR 2D - NOTRE EUROPE POUR DEMAIN
projects.action_type: Jean Monnet Actions in Other Fields of Education and Training - Learning EU initiatives
projects.objective:
OUR EUROPE FOR TOMORROW -  AVENIR 2D Project 
Despite being too often unknown, the European Union is part of our students' daily lives, offering them essential values and numerous opportunities for personal and professional development. Bearing this in mind, our school is involved in the AVENIR 2D project (Apprenons à Vivre l'Europe, échangeons Nos Idées Responsables).
This Jean Monnet project aims to strengthen European citizenship and to raise students' awareness of the values and challenges of the European Union, focusing on sustainable development in particular.
The project is built along two compatible approaches : integrating European topics into the curriculum, and offering learning experiences through a renewed Club Europe, made possible by the Jean Monnet Action, now reachable to all students from general, technological and vocational high schools altogether. 
Organized along two progressive paths, Club Europe will offer students a variety of cross disciplinary projects such as game designing, photojournalism experience, awareness-raising filmmaking, radio broadcasting, simulated decision-making exercises at the European Parliament, as well as educational trips to Europe.

projects.objective:
<< Background >>

Agri-food sector is one of the biggest and most supported sectors in the EU and a key sector for sustainable economic development, food safety and security. Despite of a huge support to farmers through its backbone - EU Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), agricultural sectors in Member States face serious problems. Project starts from important and irreplaceable role of agriculture and food industry in national economies of Member States, ensuring their food security under conditions given by CAP.

<< Objectives >>

To comprehend nature of problems in agriculture and rural areas and to be able to find appropriate solutions, students need to understand essentials of CAP. The objective is to create the Centre of Excellence providing students with the best conditions to satisfy their needs concerning studies of the CAP and its influence on all stakeholders in agriculture and rural areas. CAP is a central topic, together with short food supply chains - an innovative component from the methodology perspective.

projects.objective:
The New Paradigm for EU-Korea Relations is the basic concept of the Centre at HUFS. To provide a comprehensive answer to the concept, it is necessary to understand the new paradigm that has changed international society. Competition in the global power structure is intensifying and the new Cold War is taking place, and conflicts between camps have intensified amid the Covid-19 pandemic under the format of multipolarity.

In this context where the paradigm shift of the new international relations is underway, the current relationship between the EU and Korea needs to be upgraded, which can be largely divided into bilateral, regional and global dimensions.

projects.title_en: InclEU - Inclusivity and Challenges of the Digital Revolution in the European Union.
projects.objective:
The Jean Monnet Centre of Excellence INCLEU (Inclusivity and Challenges of the Digital Revolution in the European Union) at the University of Naples Federico II will focus on researching and disseminating knowledge about inclusivity in the European Union, with particular attention to the challenges posed by the digital revolution. 
The Centre aims to strengthen the visibility of European Union studies, foster dialogue between academics and practitioners, stimulate excellence in research and teaching, spread knowledge about the EU to the wider public, and reduce the digital divide. 
The project will offer a range of academic and public literacy activities, including conferences, seminars, courses, workshops, and publications, targeting university students, the academic community, the general public, and underserved communities.  
The Centre will leverage partnerships with local, national, and international organizations to maximize its impact and ensure the sustainability of its activities beyond the project lifecycle.

The KU Jean Monnet Centre of Excellence (KU JMCE) at Korea University aims to be a leading hub for EU-related academic activities, outreach, and researcher networking. Since its establishment in 2019, KU JMCE has been a key player in European Studies, promoting academic exchange between the EU and South Korea, and contributing to the EU studies network in the Asia-Pacific region.
Building on this success, the KU JMCE is expanding its focus to security collaboration between Europe and Korea. This project, titled "Enhancing Security Partnership Between the EU and Korea" addresses the growing security ties between Europe and Northeast Asia, driven by global challenges such as Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. South Korea’s increasing engagement with the EU and NATO, especially through the NATO+IP4 framework, highlights its expanded role in global security. Additionally, North Korea’s alliance with Russia and its advancing nuclear and missile capabilities raise concerns about regional security, underscoring the need for stronger EU-Korea cooperation.

projects.title_en: AGENDA - Approaching and exploring the EU’s fabric of policy-initiation
projects.objective: AGENDA invites students, citizens and practitioners to explore the EU’s hybrid fabric of governance and future strands for developing its democratic decision-making processes. Building on research with regard to the early phases of the EU’s policy cycle and the EU treaties’ normative setting on policy initiation and the right of legislative initiative, AGENDA looks at existing and possible opportunity structures for legislative agenda-setting and –shaping in the EU. projects.title_en: AGORA - Managing Online Extreme and Abusive Speech
projects.objective:
Managing Online Extreme and Abusive Speech (AGORA) explores problematic cases of speech (hate speech, racism, homotransphobic discourse, Holocaust denialism, fake news etc.) on social media, and their implications for individual rights as well as for the democratic fabric of contemporary societies. It seeks to identify how extreme and abusive speech spreads on social media, explores the ways in which it negatively affects democratic societies, and aims to identify strategies for mitigating these negative impacts on individual rights and the democratic fabric of our societies.
The need to analyse the phenomenon of online extreme and abusive speech, and to support national and EU institutions in elaborating policy and legislative strategies to countenance it, is the primary motivation for devising AGORA. AGORA proposes a comprehensive academic experience composed of teaching, research and dissemination activities, aimed at university students, professionals working in the relevant fields (law, journalism, human rights activism, civil service etc.), and the interested general public.

projects.title_en: RAEVC - Regulating Africa-EU Value Chains
projects.objective: Regulatory measures implementing the European Green Deal aim to address, through regulations (deforestation, minerals, due diligence, CBAM), the EU global footprint while raising environmental protection standards in third States. As the EU is dependent upon the import of resources and commodities from Africa, will these measures be enough to enable the EU to tackle its footprint and will they contribute to raise the level of environmental protection in African countries? To answer these questions, the RAEVC Chair aims to foster new teaching and excellence in research. The Chair evolves around three key themes relevant for the strengthening of the EU’s role in western and central Africa: (1) reducing the EU’s footprint by regulating the environmental and climate impact of value chains of products and commodities; (2) enhancing sustainability; (3) promoting free and fair trade.  Based at the Université Saint-Louis – Bruxelles (USL-B), the Chair will be delivered at undergraduate and post-master levels in Laws, and in the master in European Studies, for a total of 375 hours over 3 years (2024-2027). projects.title_en: CE4INT - Circular Economy for the Internal Market
projects.objective: The proposed Jean Monnet Chair “Circular Economy for the Internal Market” (CE4INT) aims to operate in the framework of the 2019 European Green Deal and the 2020 European Circular Economy Strategy. The European Union’s action for promoting the circular economy involves a reorganization of European value chains with a transformation from a linear logic of production and consumption to a circular one. In order to support this gradual but irreversible process, the EU has to rethink its policies and regulations in the coming years, encouraging the transition to the circular economy, both in terms of production and consumption. Moreover, the EU’s actions must be in line with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development of the United Nations and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), in particular SDG 12, dedicated to responsible production and consumption. Within this framework, the proposed project aims to analyze the impact of the transition to the circular economy on the European Internal Market. projects.title_en: ShapESCoLA - Shaping European Society through Constitutional Law and Access to Justice
projects.objective:
Article 2 TEU enshrines fundamental values that unify the otherwise heterogeneous, tangled EU social and political fabric. Their defence and study become increasingly relevant in light of contemporary crises – the Euro, migrations, pandemic, wars and rule of law challenges. The CJEU, in key rulings against Hungary and Poland, has affirmed that these values “define the very identity of the European Union as a common legal order”.
Yet, a growing detachment between these purportedly “top-down” values and EU citizens threatens their legitimacy, particularly amid global uncertainties. This Chair seeks to bridge the gap by conceptualising the “society” of Article 2 TEU – a European “society” – as the keystone of EU integration, to be built through a bottom-up trend, led by cooperative dialogue between courts at various levels of jurisdiction. Understanding constitutional foundations, implications for active European citizenship and limits, too, of such a peculiar “collective singular” concept is thus essential. This mission is hereby proposed to be pursued through academic research – in particular, through the lens of constitutional law.

projects.title_en: EUMEMBER - The "Member State" as a core institution of the EU
projects.objective: In 1999, the EU embarked on a quest to formulate an official motto. It was to be decided through a competition in which secondary schools across the EU could submit a proposal. In varietate concordia – or United in Diversity- became the winning submission. The motto highlights that a common purpose can be attained while embracing the diversity of the member states and their peoples. In EU studies, knowledge about the institutions, the laws and politics that binds us together has developed extensively. Any course on the EU will educate students on the process by which the union was created or the institutions through which such joint decisions continue to be made. The “United” part of the motto takes centre stage in both the teaching and research on the EU. By contrast, far less attention is devoted to explore and foster our understanding of the diversity of the current and future member states. This Jean Monnet chair aims to address this omission by developing and promoting an alternative didactic to teach EU integration. projects.title_en: European Union Development Policy in International Context
projects.objective: The module on ‘European Union Development Policy in International Context’ engaged students with the EU, utilising an innovative approach and drawing heavily on up-to-date research and current events of international significance to demonstrate how the European Union is an increasingly important international actor in the multipolar world, and a relevant and important actor for both developed and developing countries. By explicitly linking European Union Studies with Development Studies, the module was designed both to appeal to students beyond the core EU Studies discipline, and to demonstrate the relevance of studying the Union in the wider global context. This latter is of particular importance for New Zealand-based students. The European Union has traditionally been viewed in New Zealand as an important trading partner, particularly for agricultural produce. Although this was certainly true in the 1970’s, the relationship has evolved a great deal in the intervening years to become the multifaceted structure that it is today, rooted in a framework of shared values. projects.title_en: European Union External Environmental Policy
projects.objective: The European Union (EU) has a hugely important effect on the way in which environmental policies are framed and implemented not just in Europe but in many different parts of the world. After 40 years of continuous development, the environmental sector is one of the most successful and popular aspects of EU integration. However, as internal EU environmental policy reaches a stage of relatively maturity, attention is beginning to focus on how the EU can influence the governance of environmental issues not only inside but also outside of its borders. From this perspective the EU is increasingly engaging in a type of ‘external environmental governance’ in which it seeks to extend its environmental norms, rules and policies well beyond its legal jurisdiction through a mixture of persuasion, incentives and coercion. This ‘inside-out’ aspect of EU governance is not really new - the EU has long been exporting its innovative environmental policy ideas to the rest of the world. << Background >>

The European Union has been facing crucial challenges in different respects for several years. Since the inception of the global financial crisis, European economic policy has been often perceived as unfriendly, either by those facing more severe budget constraints or by countries with healthier economies. These feelings are reflected in the resurgence of populisms and neo-nationalisms. With the COVID19 crisis, the EU has gained increased awareness on the need of building a stronger Union.

<< Objectives >>

To head on toward a deeper Union, it is critical to promote the study of the impact achieved by the European economic policy and rise knowledge and consciousness on the benefits of cooperation among European countries to face the challenges of a globalized economy. Despite the EU’s global and local importance, it lacks visibility in New Zealand's (NZ) media as well as teaching and learning programmes. Given the geographical distance and historical connections with the UK, the EU, its institutions and global work are not normally discussed in NZ classrooms. Although The ‘New Zealand Curriculum' sets the general direction for teaching and learning in NZ schools, teachers are encouraged to develop their own programmes of learning and achievement objectives.

projects.title_en: Inclusion/Inklusion
projects.objective:
The project is about inclusion:
Inclusion in education is an approach to educating children with special educational needs but also the recognition of diversity and differences.
 Under the inclusion model, children with special needs spend most or all of their time with non-disabled students. Inclusion is about the child’s right to participate and the school’s duty to accept the child. Inclusion rejects the use of special schools or classrooms to separate students with disabilities from students without disabilities. A premium is placed upon full participation by students with disabilities and upon respect for their social, civil, and educational rights. 

Profile and number of participants:
Trainees for nursery school teachers in their second year. Expected Number of participants in 2014/15: 35

Aims and expected results:
Inclusion in education has developed in Germany. England and Ireland have a longer tradition on inclusion. Can German „Kindergärten“ learn  from that?

In the last few years, thanks to the realization of mobility projects funded by the Leonardo Da Vinci Program, Volontarimini Association has allowed 350 young people with special needs to complete professional internships in qualifying and useful working sectors, with the sole purpose of finding employment. 

The birth and realization of such projects have been achieved due to the strong request coming from associations comprised of relatives of young people with cognitive and psychological disabilities to Volontarimini. Obesity is a chronic disease that nowadays is becoming a social disease! It is caused by an oversupply of energy contained in foods in relation to the needs of the body, which results in storing excess as fat. It is crucial for both students and teachers to be aware of and acknowledge this diversity in perception and conceptual understanding that exists. To name a few: The Japanese traditions within design and arts and crafts are old and at the same time highly developed technically. A further extended cooperation is to be expected.

Die Universität Jena nimmt seit über 20 Jahren sehr aktiv am Erasmus-Programm teil. Es ist das erfolgreichste Europäische Mobilitätsprogramm und somit auch das gößte Austauschprogramm der Universität Jena, da wir hierüber jährlich ca. 280 - 300 Studierende und ca. 25 Mitabreiter/-innen ins europäische Ausland entsenden und auch fördern können. Das Erasmus+ Programm im Allgemeinen und somit auch das Projekt 2015  ist sehr wichtig für die ISM. Die ISM möchte seinen Studierenden ein äußerst internationales & praxisorientiertes Studienprofil bieten. Alle Studiengänge verfügen über einen integrierten Auslandsaufenthalt. 
Alle Vollzeit-Bachelor- und Master-Studierende absolvieren mindestens ein Auslandssemester, was somit einen Mobilitätsprozentsatz von 100% der Studierenden ausmacht. 
Im European Track (Bachelor) – der den größten Teil der Studierenden innehat – absolvieren alle Studierende im vierten Semester ein fest integriertes Auslandssemester an einer unserer europäischen Partnerhochschulen. Hierbei besteht der Großteil aus Erasmus Kooperationen. Der European Track „lebt“ sozusagen von den Erasmus Kooperationen. Das Erasmus Programm bildet das „Herzstück“ dieses Tracks. Die spiegelt sich für uns auch erneut in den Outgoing-Zahlen des Projekts 2015 wider. Der Großteil besteht aus Bachelor-Studierenden. Im Master Bereich haben unsere Studierende die Möglichkeit zwischen Europa und Übersee zu wählen. Von daher ist dies die kleinere Gruppe. This is a school project, described in the PEC (Educational Project) and part of the PE (School’s Strategic Plan). - Contribute to the acquisition of professional skills from a different view to that in our country

projects.title_en: Inklusion/Inclusion
projects.objective:
The project is about inclusion:

Inclusion in education is an approach to educating children with special educational needs but also the recognition of diversity and differences.

 Under the inclusion model, children with special needs spend most or all of their time with non-disabled students. Inclusion is about the child’s right to participate and the school’s duty to accept the child. Inclusion rejects the use of special schools or classrooms to separate students with disabilities from students without disabilities. A premium is placed upon full participation by students with disabilities and upon respect for their social, civil, and educational rights. 



Profile and number of participants:

Trainees for nursery school teachers in their second year. Expected Number of participants in 2014/15: 35



Aims and expected results:

Inclusion in education has developed in Germany. England and Ireland have a longer tradition on inclusion. Can German „Kindergärten“ learn  from that?

projects.title_en: FACING the creative industries to innovate entrepreneurship
projects.objective:
Cultural background, education, religion and language are just some of the variables characterizing the modern appearance of a business. These different "colors" lead us to the definition of the "plural" and heterogeneous enterprise, increasing the importance of an “aware” management of the human resources.
This phase of change shows up strongly in the Creative Industries economic segment, whereas the peculiar characteristics of the various sectors imply the need for training organisations, to adapt and continually modernize their contents, tools and methodologies, in order to play in a proactively and functional way their formative and support function. 
FACING offers a concrete answer to this needs, focusing on the Human Resources area as a well recognised driver of innovation and fundamental factor of creative enterprises’ competitiveness.
Long-term goal of the project is to modernize the capacity to provide training of the Italian organisations involved, generating a strong impact on the territory and contributing to the regeneration of the competitive potential of the Italian Creative Industries and Venetian in particular, thanks to the new shared knowledge and competences.
projects.topics: Enterprise, industry, SMEs and entrepreneurship; Creativity and culture; Gender equality / equal opportunities

projects.title_en: EU gives you WINGS: towards EUropean Work based learnING experienceS
projects.objective: The project EU Gives You WINGS stems from the need to strength in IVET students one of the key competences requested by the current economic context, i.e. sense of initiative and entrepreneurship. The best way to transfer such skills is through the use of experiences that encourage the learning by doing approach. Among these, a crucial role is played by learning experiences based on the Project-based Learning (PBL)  methodology and by the participation in transnational traineeships. Through PBL, which is a teaching method that organizes learning around projects, students gain knowledge and skills by investigating complex and real issues, carrying out tasks and developing project products. The transnational experiences carried out outside the friendly environment encourage the development of transversal skills such as adaptability and flexibility that are part of the skills required to develop an entrepreneurial attitude. Since several years, the members of the national consortium (ENAC, SCF, ENGIM VENETO) are trying to apply PBL methodologies within their centers, and they have recently decided to promote a joint project, based on this methodology, aiming at creating a network amon
projects.topics: Entrepreneurial learning - entrepreneurship education; International cooperation, international relations, development cooperation; Recognition, transparency, certification

Twelve students from Media and Communication at Rosthaug Upper Secondary have completed a three-week work placement at Berufsbildende Schule II (BBSII) in Göttingen, Germany, in two periods over two years. The students have experienced a fantastic journey in many respects. They have explored culture and togetherness, planned and carried out daily household chores, learnt about all sorts of printing techniques – traditional and modern, and visited workshops and businesses. They have learnt to address German teachers with “Herr Schmidt” rather than “Hey, Jorn!”, they have practised the art of being meticulous and endured hours of tedious work, relishing the satisfaction in seeing the final product suddenly appear. They have also taken shortcuts, only to find out that they had to do everything all over again. They have discovered a kind of endurance they did not know they had in them.

The Project will enable twenty-four students, who are attending the following courses: Business/Commerce, Information Technology, Fashion Design, Tourism and Managing and Events Services (from the 2nd and 3rd years – equivalent to the 11th and 12th grade) to do an international work placement in companies located in France (Clermond-Ferrand), Italy (Palermo) and Spain (Granada). Together with the EuRoPe Design Project and EmploVET (Employability & Workplace Skills for VET Students) Strategic Partnership, EuRoPe Tailors project met some of the most important needs of our organization – to learn, develop and offer better professional integration chances to students with reduced opportunities.

projects.objective:
The Auschwitz Jewish Center (AJC) is the only Jewish presence in Oświęcim – the town the Germans called  Auschwitz – which is primarily associated with the site of the darkest tragedy of the 20th century.  AJC is affiliated with the Museum of Jewish Heritage – A Living Memorial to the Holocaust in New York. 

AJC’s mission is to honor the former residents of the town and to teach future generations about the destruction caused by the Holocaust as well as modern dangers of intolerance and prejudice.

Hosting volunteers has become an essential element of our work as it contributes to developing connections between people different nationalities and cultures thus reducing mutual prejudice. The same is true in regard to the positive impact of volunteers on the local community. In addition the project contributes to fostering the idea of volunteering in the town of Oświęcim.

During this time we hosted two volunteers: Marit from Germany and Hannah from Belgium (Flemish region). Girls worked together for the benefit of our local community, primarily by sharing knowledge about other cultures with young people and teaching them to respect diversity, helping them to understand the mechanisms of function of intercultural society and an importance of learning foreign languages. Volunteers promoted the idea of EVS and encourage young people to engage in their own local and international projects. We believe that the presence of foreign volunteers in our project  inspired young people we deal with to take unconventional steps regarding their own path of development, gaining new skills and competences. It is so important for us because the recipients of the project are children and young people from rural areas, most of them have no the opportunities that their peers from cities have, they are from families that face the financial problems, from incomplete families – for many of them this project is the only opportunity to meet with other cultures.

DANCE AROUND THE WORLD is a youth exchange programme between the United Kingdom, (through NICOLA), Italy (NICOLA Italy), Spain (Asociación Xuvenil Vrenza,), France (through NICOLA) and Holland (through Untold). 
The aim of the project is to enrich young people’s knowledge of the origins of various dance styles, create items that reflect their cultural and social identity, and to encourage them to confidently voice their opinions. The young people engaged in a dance project that focuses on the theme of cultural influences in dance, and the related music, fashion and social issues. Workshops in different dance styles were held with the aim of fusing those styles in original dance productions (videos-photos). The programme was held at Vanston Community Centre and Chelsea Theatre, London.

In this youth exchange, 40 young adults interested in dance engaged in a variety of activities focused on researching dance and their features in different cultures. projects.title_en: Finding traces
projects.objective: The organizing partners of the project "Finding traces", Ludwig Wolker Haus e.V. in  Berlin and Proyecto Kieu in Numancia de la Sagra, provided an opportunity for youth with fewer opportunities in an international encounter. Twenty four youth age 14 to 19 years from Germany and Spain met in two one-week encounters in July 2016. During the photography project participants were searching for traces following various topics such as housing, food, mobility, youth life style, religion, communication etc. and commonly explored the different, metropolitan and rural, surroundings they live in. Participants were actively and result-orientated involved in all project steps. An exhibition was curated, developed and presented to the public in both countries. Organizing this public event served a major objective of the project to facilitate and support Youth in social networking and entrepreneurship. The pedagogical approach of the project  strongly focussed on identification and promotion of individual competences. The public exhibitions promoted European programs and thus opportunities of shared activities for youth in both countries.

projects.title_en: So You Have A Degree
projects.objective:
Obtaining a degree or diploma is almost a prerequisite for our youth today and the ability to freely move to other countries to study has allowed our youth to obtain education from almost any university in the world.  However, having a degree does not guarantee employment.  As a matter of fact, one of the factors that create large amounts of unemployment is the fact that so many people have degrees in the same fields.  Another issue of concern is that not all universities are recognised with the same respect in different countries.  Some universities are so well known that simply having a degree from that university could secure employment but then we realise that these universities also happen to be the most expensive thus not accessible to all.

Our project aims to look at education and the value of education, meaning the value of it when we come back to our country and the value associated with the chances of finding employment with that degree or diploma.  
We have seen that young people follow fashionable educational choices and we want to evaluate this to help young people make more informed choices regarding education so that they are more employable after their education
projects.topics: Labour market issues incl. career guidance / youth unemployment; Early School Leaving / combating failure in education; Youth (Participation, Youth Work, Youth Policy)

The aim of this project is to ensure and give continuity to the arms sector in the Basque Country. Traditional sector with a high international projection and very identified with Eibar and the country.
In recent years there has been a decrease in the production of companies belonging to this sector. This is due to the lack of productive capacity due to the lack of generational replacement.
The aim is to offer future gunsmiths specific technical training specific to the sector and demanded by companies, recovering and ensuring their own knowledge of the sector and establishing a system of permanent collaboration between the sector itself and the centre for the detection and development of new collaboration opportunities in areas such as surveillance and forecasting, advanced management, applied innovation, internationalisation, etc.
In order to give continuity to the sector it is necessary to have trained and qualified people, which is why Armeria Eskola tries to adapt vocational training to the current and future needs of the productive sectors and to the employability of people, in response to the growing need for qualification and specialisation in companies

In current times of crisis it is necessary to create opportunities to improve socio-labour conditions of EU citizens, especially regarding to
the youth unemployment that is becoming alarming.

since 2008, the total number in the EU has increased by one million. There are now over 5million young people in the EU-28 under the
age of 25, who cannot find a job.
In Italy youth unemployment exceeds 31,8% (ISTAT 2012) and in Calabria is 65%.
In 2012 in Italy over 2.250 (23,9%) young people aged 15-29 are NEET (Not in Education, Employment or Training) risking to remain
social excluded. The majority are women (26,1%). In Calabria 15,9% of the whole young population are NEET.
In this context traineeship has a key role in increasing the access into the labour market because it can fill the gap between the theory
gained in education and the skills acquisition needed by the market, because it allows youngsters to acquire and develop, both working
and transversal skills, that are crucial elements to reinforce their employment-competitiveness.

projects.title_en: Neue Inputs für den schulischen Alltag (im europäischen Ausland) gewinnen - Persönlichkeitsentwicklung
projects.objective: Als Schule sind wir auf der Suche nach neuen Ideen und Anregungen, die wir in unseren schulischen Alltag integrieren können. Außerdem wollen wir uns noch weiter europäisch mit anderen Schulen vernetzen. Außerdem schätzen wir die Persönlichkeitsentwicklung unserer SchülerInnen sowie unserer KollegInnen sehr hoch. Sehr gerne möchten wir die Personal- und Methodenkompetenz in Bezug auf die Persönlichkeitsentwicklung in anderen europäischen Ländern kennenlernen und diesen Erfahrungsschatz in die Schulgemeinschaft integrieren. Aus diesem Grund haben wir einen Kurs im Ausland gefunden, der sich thematisch mit "Neuen Impulsen für den Unterricht - Persönlichkeitsentwicklung" beschäftigt und der uns in unserer Schulentwicklung weiterbringen würde. Außerdem ist das Seminar so angelegt, dass es eine Möglichkeit der Vernetzung mit TeilnehmerInnen aus anderen EU-Ländern gibt, so dass wir auch hier Informationen zum Thema Persönlichkeitsentwicklung bekommen würden.  Diese Fortbildungsmaßnahme gewährt darüber hinaus Wissen auf dem neuesten Stand. Für die Maßnahme der Fortbildung im Bereich Persönlichkeitsentwicklung haben wir eine Teilnehmerin gewählt, die sich mit diesem Themenbereich auseinande

Modern language skills, especially English skills should be  "mobilised" - with students as much as with teaching staff and management. And also the outcomes of compulsory work placements should be evaluated more often and also in a cross-curricular approach.

projects.title_en: EuroVITO - Hoeveproducten - Vente à la ferme
projects.objective: The name of the project 'EuroVITO' refers undoubtedly to Europe and our school VITO-Hoogstraten. With this project we wanted to stimulate our students to extend their limits: geographical, to explore other countries and cultures and to be open towards other cultures and countries, but also personally to develop their own social and linguistic skills. The annex ’Hoeveproducten-Produits de la ferme’ represented the theme of this project. We strongly wanted to focus on the short food supply chain: from the field to the plate, from farmer to consumer. This sale (and processing) of farm products produced by the farmers themselves is strongly present in e.g. the French regions Lot-et-Garonne and Ardèche. Therefore, this theme was addressed extensively both during the preparation and the internship itself, but also during the postprocessing. W projekcie uczestniczyło 40 uczniów, którzy odbywali praktykę w Niemczech (Lipsk). Byli to uczniowie Zespołu Szkół Ponadgimnazjalnych nr 3 klas drugich o kierunku technik  mechanik (7), technik usług fryzjerskich (5), technik pojazdów samochodowych (14), technik budowlaniec (4) i technik elektryk (10). Staż odbywał się w maju i czerwcu i trwał 4 tygodnie. 
Głównym celem wyjazdu był rozwój zawodowy uczniów, poznanie działania firm zagranicznych związanych z ich dziedziną nauczania, porównanie metod pracy przyjętych w Polsce z metodami stosowanymi w innych krajach europejskich, nabycie umiejętności pracy w zespole międzynarodowym i poznanie innych, często nowatorskich rozwiązań mechanicznych. Ponadto uczniowie udoskonalili umiejętności językowe oraz poznali kulturę innych krajów Unii Europejskiej w tym kulturę i organizację pracy w Niemczech. Wiedza i umiejętności uczniów potwierdzone certyfikatami i dokumentem Europass Mobilność zwiększyły ich szanse na znalezienie atrakcyjnej pracy. Umiejętności nabyte podczas praktyk w Lips

projects.objective:

The college works with students from some of the most deprived areas of the city, often feeling disheartened or lacking the motivation to look for employment due to their lack of experience. projects.title_en: European Steps to Employment
projects.objective: Wolverhampton Adult Education Service strives to help young adults learn employable skills and develop behaviour and attitudes that will best equip them to enter the job market and flourish in society. Several areas of Wolverhampton are marked by high levels of multiple  deprivation and the city has suffered severely during the economic crisis. In this climate many young people and those suffering from job loss in mid-life despair and lose motivation.  They are unaware of opportunities that exist through collaboration in Europe to build a better future for themselves, seeing others  come to Wolverhampton seeking to improve their lives but feeling excluded from this type of mobility themselves.    This project will provide a uniquely motivating opportunity for students to gain first-hand experience of working in their field in two economically buoyant and forward-looking  cities in Italy.  It will also offer a change of direction for mature students needing to reinvent their careers while providing a European dimension to our suite of Steps to Employment courses that have been cited as examples of outstanding practice by OFSTED. projects.title_en: Teaching and innovation for VET in current Europe
projects.objective:
Due to:
-The difficult labor market situation in Spain where youth unemployment exceeds 50% , and  to the high dropout rates
--The Changes in the Spanish VET state regulations 
-The Changes in the production system, which requires new teaching methods that include a good understanding of work practices and that the labor market is no longer confined to national territory but expands to neighboring countries.

This mobility project for teachers and management staff is needed so they can be aware of the needs of the European labor market, make contact with new approaches and take a more active and participatory role in the places where they perform their teaching work.

Moreover, teachers and management staff need to establish long-term European networks of knowledge that will allow them to reach:

-Companies.
-Educative centers.
-Social agents.
-Local authorities.

This will give them the opportunity to be in touch with innovation, know about other educational and productive systems, share the best practices, and improve their knowledge on what European policies are being implemented. All that will lead to an improvement in the quality of the work being done in schools

projects.title_en: Freiwilligenaustausch mit Partnerstädten 2016/17
projects.objective: The volunteer exchanges between twinned cities is a two-way exchange: Young people commit themselves to carry out full-time voluntary work in social, cultural, ecological or sports associations and organisations. The volunteers combine their service with a long-term stay abroad (6 to 12 months). Young people from Cologne visit one of our partner cities, while young people from these cities come to Köln. The cities involved are Cologne and some of its partners: Barcelona (Spain), Beijing (China), Cluj-Napoca (Rumänien), Cork (Ireland), Esch zur Alzette (Luxembourg), Istanbul (Turkey), Katowice (Poland), Lille (France), Liverpool (UK), Rotterdam (the Netherlands), Tel Aviv (Israel), Thessaloniki (Greece) and Wolgograd (Russia). Disadvantaged young people would also be involved. The result will thus be an intercultural exchange at different levels – between German and foreign young people living in Cologne, between young people with different levels of education, and between young people from Cologne and from its partner cities – all learning and working together. projects.objective: Europe is currently witnessing the largest and most rapid escalation ever in the number of people being forced from their homes. The so called “European migrant crisis” or “European refugee crisis” began in 2015, when a rising number of refugees and migrants made the journey to the European Union to seek asylum, travelling across the Mediterranean Sea, or through the eastern borders of Europe. Howewer, Europe is facing since years the issues related to refugees and asylum seekers and to the integration of migrants in the European countries' social fabric. projects.title_en: SCHOOL UNDER OAKS
projects.objective:
“School Under Oaks” to roczny Wolontariat Europejski zrealizowany przez Gminę Dąbrowa wraz z wolontariuszką Seher Yumrutepe z Turcji.
Projekt był odpowiedzią na zidentyfikowane potrzeby lokalnej społeczności niespełna pięciotysięcznej wiejskiej gminy, w której starsi i młodsi borykają się z problemem bariery językowej. Głównym tematem projektu było nauczanie języka angielskiego z zastosowaniem metod pozaformalnych. projects.title_en: Nachhaltigkeit: Wie wollen wir leben?
projects.objective: Climatic change, environmental degradation and other related issues that will affect the future have been facing the same dilemma for many years: The knowledge of the problems and the ensuing problems is publicly known and has been widely discussed. However, only a limited proportion of the population acts accordingly (i.e. in a way required to solve these problems). A look at the development of the last decades reveals that neither the problems nor the proposed solutions have changed. Sustainable development cannot be achieved on the sole basis of proposals of the economic and political elites or of new technologies. It also requires social change and cultural responsibility. Education is an important approach in this context in order to enable and motivate the citizens to participate in political and democratic action. It is therefore even more important to study this theme with young adults in a European context in order to raise their awareness of the cross-border and global dimension of this issue. Elle s’explique d’une part par la place des études consacrées aux aires culturelles à l’EHESS et par la dimension résolument comparative de notre tradition scientifique, et d’autre part par la multiplicité de nos relations avec les universités et centres de recherche à l’étranger et de nos programmes d’invitations et d'échanges. 

Le programme Erasmus+ complète un dispositif de formation à dimension européenne existant comme le Master Erasmus Mundus TEMA European Territories: Identity and Development, mis en place en 2011 et renouvelé en juin 2017 sous le titre TEMA+ European Territories: Heritage and Development. Les relations avec l’Allemagne sont renforcées par les doubles-diplômes franco-allemands labellisés UFA : Master Histoire et civilisations, en partenariat avec l’Université de Heidelberg, Master Anthropologie, en partenariat avec l’Université Johann Wolfgang Goethe de Francfort ou au niveau doctoral, le Collège doctoral franco-allemand, en partenariat avec l’Université Humboldt

projects.objective:
Transhumance Livestock Farming is a traditional farming system with a long history, especially in the countries around the Mediterranean Sea. This system is based on a seasonal rotation of the pasture, between valleys and lowlands in winter and mountain pastures in the summer. In this way, animals cover their nutrition needs from grazing, thus utilizing a large amount of grazing land that would otherwise be untapped, contributing at the same time to shaping the landscape and playing an important role in local culture.
The aim of the mobility program was the theoretical and practical training of 15 trainees from the region of Epirus who work and support technically the Transhumance Livestock Farming.
Thirteen trainees are young shepherd breeders, members of ATSE, who are also engaged in or want to deal with the processing of their products.
Two are Animal Scientists, holders of a corresponding Postgraduate, employees of the Center for Animal Genetic Resources of Ioannina, who have been supporting the pastoral livestock farming in recent years.
The training took place in Southern France, an area with a long tradition in the seasonal transhumance of animals, from 17 to 28/09/2018.

Companies and social agents should participate in the conception and the learning-teaching process in Vocational Training at all levels, as it has been proved in the Dual system of learning. Vocational Training must encompass work combined as long as possible with an international experience.

projects.title_en: DESIDERIUS PRO
projects.objective:
The academic consortium Desiderius Pro has been set up to address the following issues:
- The low rate of students doing mobility abroad in vocational training high schools of the Academy of Rennes.
- The lack of an academic consortium of mobility in education and vocational training
- The evolution of student audiences
- The need to strengthen institutional relations with the economic community
- The desire for greater European openness, on an academic scale.
The objectives of the project were:
For learners: the acquisition of professional, cognitive, technical, social and linguistic skills, the acquisition of a European awareness, an increased self-esteem.
For teachers and employees o national educations: immerse themselves in the practices of European partners in the company and in schools, to integrate them to meet the demands of the job market and bring new educational responses.
The agreed project provided 200 mobilities over 2 years: 148 mobilities for learners, 52 for staff. The 11 high schools of the consortium were able to achieve more mobility than expected: 157 pupils mobility and 62 teachers mobility.

projects.title_en: Creating opportunities for all to become actors of Europe
projects.objective:
Context of the project

Myriam secondary vocational school hosts 435 students aged 15-24 in Toulouse. Students are offered vocational trainings in "Fashion-related jobs", "Business", "User and customer services reception" and "Collective catering" from CAP (EQF level 3) to BTS (EQF level 5) . A class for vocational preparation helps young people with frequent educational difficulties in search of a professional project to find out those trainings and sometimes integrate them. Work experience placements are compulsory for all our sections. We also welcome students with disabilities who are supported by a special needs unit (ULIS) and integrated into the training of their choice.  



Objectives

We wish to move into the process of European opening the Erasmus+ project offers us to implement. The first objective of our project is to provide our trainings with an innovative and formative momentum, evolve to give our students wider and more constructive opportunities and enable them to get a vision of the professional world with skills exchanges and innovative learnings. The school also includes an educational training company: "Chocobois", an international exchange service.
The students are between 15 and 19 years old. Most of them come from rural areas,and they are not sufficiently prepared to meet the demands of a tertiary sector that is developing widely internationally.

 VET system has played a main role in fighting these challenges over the years, however in order to continue to tackle early school leaving and equipping students with relevant skills required by the labour market, it is important to foster WBL practices.
 Moving from these challenges and considering that the Italian Ministry of Labour and Social Policy launched the Dual System in Italy, the members of the consortium have decided to increase the opportunities for learning mobility during VET pathways that use WBL methodologies.

Indeed, WBL and transnational mobility experiences are important to (re)motivate VET learners (preventing early school leaving) and to provide them with the competences required by the companies.

projects.title_en: WE RURAL
projects.objective:
At present, 75% of the EU population lives in urban areas, while over 90% of its territory is classified as rural. These rural areas throughout Europe are often neglected and portrayed in a negative way. Wether we like or not, the image of the “rural” is  generally associated with the rustic, old-fashioned and poor, and its inhabitants face isolation, lack of infrastructure and services and a restricted job market. For this reason, rural young people are often stereotyped as bored, lacking ambition or troublemakers.
 However, new technologies, bio values and examples of young entrepreneurship and sustainable innovation in the countryside redefine what “rural” means and provide a modern and fresh look at rural areas in Europe today.

Our partners were two Informal Groups of Young People – “Folklór a Zábava” form the Czech Republic and “FS Krtísan” from Slovakia. projects.title_en: Good Bye Job Hello Career
projects.objective:
With youth unemployment reaching over 45% in most EU countries we see that young people try to get the best education simply to secure a job, but is a job enough, what happened to searching for the right career?

This youth exchange focused on helping young people to identify their skills and competences in order for them to plan for careers rather than jobs which will simply pay the bills.  We have empowered young people to identify their skills and talents and to plan for their careers while understanding the needs of the labour markets and making sure they find a solid standing in their labour markets with a long-lasting career that can offer them a more secure future.

We explored main complaint that there is no link between their education and the labour market, and we have researched this even deeper and have discovered that there is no link between their skills and abilities and their plans for their future.  Most young people follow fashionable career paths through education without planning their future or even knowing what the future, in terms of employment, can offer them and as a result we see very high number in youth unemployment all over the world. projects.objective:
Challenging behaviour can be defined as when the behaviour of a person puts themselves and those around them at risk, leads to a poorer quality of life or is socially unacceptable. It can also impact on person’s ability to join in everyday activities. Communication is the main way we interact and express our needs, likes and dislikes. If communication is a problem, it can be very frustrating for the person and may result in challenging behaviour. Challenging behaviour is often seen in people coming from a difficult background  or in people with conditions that affect communication and the brain such as learning disabilities and mental health problems.  
 
 A person with challenging behaviour is not a ‘problem’ to be fixed and is not doing something ‘wrong’. However, behaviour is a sign that something is not working. It shows that there is some unfulfilled need or a problem with communication. It is not always easy to identify this lacuna making it difficult for the professionals working with them. projects.title_en: Joint European Master in Tribology of Surfaces and Interfaces
projects.objective: Tribology is the science of interacting surfaces in relative motion. These interactions take place between surfaces of materials, and so control friction, wear and lubrication behavior. Understanding the nature of these interactions on the macro, micro and nano scales and solving the technological problems associated with interfacial phenomena are the very essence of tribology. The subject of tribology matters because so much of the world’s energy, the majority of which is produced from non-renewable resources, is consumed in overcoming friction and replacing prematurely worn components. Many studies have shown that lessening the amount of energy used in this way is one of best ways we can reduce our impact on environment.Tribology incorporates many disciplines, including mechanical engineering, materials science, mechanics, surface chemistry and physics and a multitude of subjects, such as surface characterization, friction, wear, lubrication, thin films, coatings, materials, lubricants and selection and design of lubrication systems and contact properties. The subject of tribology is at the core of engineering science and is now one of its most dynamic and rapidly advancing areas

Andererseits bieten englischsprachige Lehrveranstaltungen die Grundlage eines breiten Angebots für internationale Studierende, die nicht über deutsche Sprachkenntnisse verfügen. Wir arbeiten daran, dass dies an unserer Universität weiter ausgebaut und so noch attraktiver für Incomings wird.

La participation de l’EHESS au programme Erasmus + renforce la dimension internationale de l’école. L’internationalisation est en effet une caractéristique fondamentale de la formation à l’EHESS. Elle s’explique d’une part par la place des études consacrées aux aires culturelles à l’EHESS et par la dimension résolument comparative de notre tradition scientifique, et d’autre part par la multiplicité de nos relations avec les universités et centres de recherche à l’étranger et de nos programmes d’invitations et d'échanges.

Le programme Erasmus+ complète un dispositif de formation à dimension européenne existant comme le Master Erasmus Mundus TEMA European Territories: Identity and Development, mis en place en 2011 et renouvelé en juin 2017 sous le titre TEMA+ European Territories: Heritage and Development. Ce projet est né en 1997, date à laquelle PROMOTRANS, association de formation patronale créé à l’initiative de syndicats de transporteurs routiers et spécialisée dans la formation d’étudiants/apprenants, de salariés et de chefs d’entreprises dans les secteurs des transports, de la logistique et de la chaîne globale d’approvisionnement, a souhaité internationaliser le cursus de sa première école d’enseignement supérieur, l’Ecole Européenne des Transports (EET) en participant au premier programme de mobilité LEONARDO. En mai 2006, une étudiante de l’EET a été choisie par la Commission Européenne comme Ambassadrice Leonardo Da Vinci pour la France pour l’excellence de son placement transnational lors d’une cérémonie à Graz (Autriche). En 2007, PROMOTRANS s’est constitué en Consortium coordonnant et pilotant le projet de mobilité de stages pour les écoles rebaptisées ECOLES INTERNATIONALES DES TRANSPORTS ET DE LA LOGISTIQUE (EITL) et titulaires de la Charte ERASMUS pour 7 ans puis renouvelée pour 7 ans jusqu’en 2020. Celui-ci a obtenu le certificat pour l’organisation de stages ERASMUS par les Consortiums (CHOSE) de 2008 à 2011 puis de 2011 à 2017.

projects.objective:
Główne cele Programu Erasmus+ realizowanego w naszej uczelni to:
1. podniesienie stopnia umiędzynarodowienia uczelni poprzez rozwijanie współpracy z partnerami zagranicznymi,
2. zwiększenie mobilności międzynarodowej studentów oraz pracowników naukowych i administracyjnych,
3. wymiana dobrych praktyk i doświadczeń,
4. rozwój programów studiów w języku angielskim,
5. uwrażliwianie i uświadamianie społeczności akademickiej w kontekście funkcjonowania uczelni w szeroko pojętym świecie akademickim UE, w tym w odniesieniu do wielokulturowości, komunikacji międzykulturowej, potrzeby stałego doskonalenia się (np. językowego) i otwartości na innych.
W projekcie wzięło udział odpowiednio:
- SMS - 2
- SMP - 10 (w tym 2 studentów ze stypendium zerowym)
- STA - 4
- STT - 3
W porównaniu z poprzednim rokiem akademickim odnotowaliśmy znaczący wzrost zainteresowania wyjazdami SMP, który był efektem podejmowanych działań promocyjno-informacyjnych, a głównie spotkań organizowanych przez Sekcję Programu Erasmus, podczas których stypendyści programu opowiadali studentom o swoich wrażeniach i doświadczeniach z wyjazdów. Studenci i pracownicy naszej uczelni brali udział w mobilności edukacyjn

projects.objective:
Uczelnia w roku 2018 , przy udziale przebudowanego biura Erasmus+ kontynuuje rozwój współpracy międzynarodowej, czego jednym z wieku aspektów jest rozwój mobilności pracowników i studentów w ramach programu Erasmus+.
Zmiany organizacyjne z roku 2016 oraz szeroko zakrojona akcja informacyjna pozwoliła zainteresować programem Erasmus+ więcej studentów i pracowników z coraz większym sukcesem.
Główne cele jakościowe i ilościowe to dopasowanie ilości organizowanych wyjazdów do potencjału uczelni i studentów. Jest to proces długotrwały i wielowątkowy polegający na:
- rozwoju sieci uczelni partnerskich
- dopracowywaniu procedur,
- poinformowaniu studentów o możliwościach i zasadach programu
- poinformowaniu studentów o osiągnięciach innych studentów podczas ich wyjazdów i ich wrażeniach
- podziale pracy tak, aby dopełnić wszystkich formalności związanych z organizacją wyjazdów i przyjazdów
każdego rodzaju
W ciągu 2 lat  udało nam się zdecydowanie poprawić wskaźniki dot. mobilności.
W porównaniu z 2017 rokiem zwiększyliśmy liczbę wyjazdów ze 122 do 185 w wyniku dobrze przeprowadzonej akcji rekrutacyjnej, oraz wymiany doświadczeń przez wracających studentów i pracowników z innymi.

Projekt Programu Erasmus+ AK103 mobilność edukacyjna realizowany w roku akademickim 2018/19 był jednym z głównych sposobów realizacji strategii umiędzynarodowienia na Uniwersytecie Marii Curie-Skłodowskiej. W projekcie realizowano wymianę studentów i pracowników z uczelniami z krajów programu oraz wyjazdy studentów na praktyki zawodowe do krajów programu. 
Celem działań realizowanych przez uczelnię było zwiększenie poziomu umiędzynarodowienia Uczelni oraz jakości kształcenia zgodnie ze Strategią Rozwoju Uczelni. Główne cele jakościowe i ilościowe projektu zostały osiągnięte. Realizacja wymian odbywała się na podstawie porozumień programu Erasmus+ mobilność edukacyjna z partnerami w krajach programu.

projects.objective:
Akademia Techniczno-Humanistyczna w Bielsku-Białej realizowała działania o charakterze mobilnościowym uwzględnione w ramach umowy finansowej numer 2018-1-PL01-KA103-047860 w roku akademickim 2018/2019 i 2019/2020. Kontrakt, przedłużony ze względu na pandemię COVID-19  o kolejne dwanaście miesięcy, czyli do 31 maja 2021 roku, pozwolił na realizację wyjazdów w kategoriach:
- podjęcia części kształcenia w uczelni partnerskiej – wyjazdy na studia (SMS) w liczbie 14
- wyjazdu studentów w celu odbycia praktyk – wyjazdy na praktyki (SMP)  w liczbie 26
- wyjazdy nauczycieli w celach dydaktycznych – wyjazdy z wykładami (STA)  w liczbie 55
- wyjazdy pracowników akademickich w celach szkoleniowych (STT)  w liczbie 88.

Studenci uczestniczący w wymianie zarówno w uczelni macierzystej jak i pozostałych podmiotach mieli możliwość podniesienia nie tylko kompetencji edukacyjnych, ale także kulturowych – w tym bardzo istotnych dla przyszłego rozwoju zawodowego – kompetencji językowych. Ponadto wyjazdy studenckie pozwoliły studentom na przełamanie barier społecznych, rozwój interpersonalny oraz budowę kapitału społecznego jeszcze przed ukończeniem toku studiów. projects.action_type: Higher education student and staff mobility within programme countries
projects.objective:
Szkoła Główna Turystyki i Hotelarstwa Vistula (SGTiH Vistula) jest jedną  z  najbardziej  umiędzynarodowionych uczelni o profilu turystycznym w Polsce i stawia na ciągły rozwój. Jako pierwsza w Polsce zdobyła akredytację THE-ICE (The International Centre of Excellence in Tourism and Hospitality Education). Jest to jeden z dwóch najważniejszych na świecie certyfikatów przyznawanych uczelniom kształcącym na potrzeby branż zajmujących się turystyką, rekreacją, organizacją wydarzeń i sztuką kulinarną. Jest znakiem najwyższej jakości kształcenia i prestiżu.
Internacjonalizacja jest jednym z filarów strategii rozwoju Uczelni, a  Program Erasmus+  jest ważnym elementem tego procesu. Dzięki współpracy w obszarze szkolnictwa wyższego na poziomie europejskim SGTiH Vistula jest w stanie zrealizować zamierzenia zawarte w misji i strategii oraz następujące cele: 
•	elastyczne dostosowanie oferty dydaktycznej do potrzeb międzynarodowego rynku pracy z nastawieniem na potrzeby sektora czasu wolnego i działających w nim jednostek z naciskiem na przedsiębiorczość, innowacyjność, wiedzę, umiejętności oraz kompetencje zawodowe absolwentów, 
•	internalizacja programu kształcenia, rozwój obcojęzyczny

projects.title_en: Higher education student and staff mobility project
projects.action_type: Higher education student and staff mobility within programme countries
projects.objective: Zrealizowany projekt dotyczył mobilności studentów i pracowników uczelni między krajami programu. Głównym celem projektu było pogłębianie współpracy międzynarodowej oraz internacjonalizacja procesu kształcenia. Poprzez zrealizowaną mobilność podtrzymano współpracę między uczelniami biorącymi udział w projekcie. Wymiana doświadczeń, zapoznanie się z dobrymi praktykami pozwoliła na uatrakcyjnienie kształcenia. Ze względu na okres pandemii w programie wziął udział tylko jeden nauczyciel akademicki.Mobilność dotyczyła prowadzenia zajęć na uczelni w Estonii. Celem było w tym przypadku zdobycie specjalistycznej wiedzy na uczelni posiadającej duże doświadczenie w obszarze międzykulturowości. Było to spowodowane zwiększaniem się z okresu na okres liczby studentów cudzoziemców głównie z obszaru Rosji, Białorusi, Kazachstanu. Cel ten został zrealizowany a doświadczenia przeniesione na praktykę. Pandemia uniemożliwiła zrealizowanie pozostałych mobilności, planowani uczestnicy wycofali się z obawy przed konsekwencjami zachorowania. Nawet akcja szczepień nie zmieniły nastawienia potencjalnych uczestników mobilności.

projects.objective:
W roku akademickim 2018/2019 i do końca maja 2020 r. w ramach działań sektorowych "Szkolnictwo wyższe" zrealizowano projekt mobilności studentów i pracowników Wyższej Szkoły Policji w Szczytnie. Współpraca z uczelniami europejskimi, wymiana pracowników i studentów, realizacja wspólnych przedsięwzięć i projektów naukowych stanowi integralną część działalności Szkoły, wpisaną w jej aktualną strategię. Wszelkie  podejmowane tym zakresie działania przedstawicieli społeczności akademickiej mają przyczynić się do poprawy jakości nauczania, rozwoju badań oraz tworzenia innowacyjnych programów kształcenia, dopasowanych do wymagań i potrzeb współczesnych europejskich realiów społecznych, gospodarczych czy technologicznych

o	broadenging the perspectives of the school’s leadership,

projects.title_en: Inclusion
projects.objective:
The project is about inclusion:
 Inclusion in education is an approach to educating children with special educational needs but also the recognition of diversity and differences.
  Under the inclusion model, children with special needs spend most or all of their time with non-disabled students. Inclusion is about the child’s right to participate and the school’s duty to accept the child. Inclusion rejects the use of special schools or classrooms to separate students with disabilities from students without disabilities. A premium is placed upon full participation by students with disabilities and upon respect for their social, civil, and educational rights. 
 
 Profile and number of participants:
 Trainees for nursery school teachers in their second year. Expected Number of participants from 2018-2019: 45

 Inclusion in education has developed in Germany. England and Ireland have a longer tradition on inclusion. Can German „Kindergärten“ learn  from that?

projects.title_en: Being European, a solution for tomorrow
projects.objective:
Our many years of work experiences abroad with Erasmus+ has reinforced the importance of developing a European dimension to our projects, to improve the quality of our educational offerings towards unmotivated, struggling, and sometimes dropout students. These projects contribute to a collective reflection within our disciplinary teams, reflection which is based on the spreading of knowledge, the European and citizen dimension, and equal opportunity for men and women. These different themes will be developed in the new school project, which is currently being drafted.
 
 These work experiences abroad are sources of personal enrichment, which contribute to an openness towards others and a renewed motivation for the various participants. projects.objective:
The current European Voluntary Service program, entitled "Step out of your comfort zone", is part of the Youth Initiatives in Action program and will be implemented by Iasis NGO in Athens with a duration of 6 months. Ten (10) applicants, aged 18 to 30, coming from Spain, France and Italy will be occupied.
 The main objective of the program is to give young people from different countries the opportunity to identify the needs of vulnerable social groups and minorities (eg mentally ill, asylum-seekers, single parent families, etc.) and an active role in limiting this phenomenon. To develop their personality, increase job opportunities and become part of the multidisciplinary consolidation of Greek society. Additionally, those attending and corresponding career paths will gain experience in real-world working environment, such as keeping hours, as well as implementing small programs over a certain period of time. The professional and personal skills they will receive are one of the program's primary objectives. At a wider level, participants will experience themselves in an experience that only positive elements and knowledge can offer on both a professional and a personal level.

projects.title_en: Freiheit oder Sicherheit oder beides? In welchem Europa wollen wir leben? (Teil I)
projects.objective:
The discussion about freedom and security has reached new dimensions at European level in the last years and dominates our daily debates. Prevention of terrorism, rule of law, martial law, surveillance states or border security: Personal convictions regarding freedom and security are values that pose a great risk to trigger value-based conflicts in socio-political debates and therefore social conflicts. They pose a risk for a united and free Europe, as re-erected physical borders find their way into the citizens' minds. For many people, this discussion of freedom and security is characterized by an “either-or”, where they have to weigh the two options in a zero-sum game. Currently, the pendulum swings towards security, a loss of freedom seems to be acceptable for many people. But does it really have to be an either-or, or is there a reasonable compromise? This is a very individual decision that we base on personal as well as cultural values. A decisive yes or no, a black or white thinking is dangerous for peaceful coexistence within society, as individual opinions are delegitimized. It is much rather about careful considerations, intuition and sensitivity.

projects.title_en: Sewing a network: electronic textiles in educational making workshops
projects.objective:
For almost a decade, the maker movement has been making its own may into non-formal education. Educators and researchers have been talking about the role of making activities in learning; they highlight the potential for project-based and hands-on approach to boost youth interest for inquiry and learning, to re-activate them from a social, psychological, professional point of view.
 One popular strand of making activities in the context of non formal education involve experimenting with computer
 programming, electronics, and robotics.
 Typically, girls are much less prone to participate in such initiatives than boys, mainly due to the negative stereotypes they nurture towards scientific and technical disciplines. Thus, the great promise of the maker movement to democratize access to making as well as to its progressive spirit and philosophy are to be reconsidered in the face of evidence. If we believe that making activities and maker identities are crucial for empowerment, then it is our job to set up situations whereby all learners have the opportunity and will to engage.
 E-textiles promises to be the trojan horse that will enable girls to fully benefit from making activitie

Today young people face new challenges related to the interconnectivity of people and countries around the world. The recent trends of globalisation make a significant impact on the lives of youth and the local communities they belong to. Dependency on issues in other regions and increasing diversity in a local society requires rethinking what new competences young people need nowadays. Furthermore, current trends require a more active civic participation of youngsters towards meeting challenges of the global society including the growing inequality, injustice and climate change.

This can only happen when young people perceive themselves not only as citizens of their country but as citizens of the world. projects.objective:
The „Borderlands of Culture” project assumed an organization of a multilevel activity of two groups of young people form Poland (Białystok) and Ukraine (Łuck), all of them folklore enthusiasts. Our project had a clear goal – to prove that the cultures of neighboring countries have great influence on each other, even if they are divided by a strong, formal border. Apart from that we focused on finding common elements of cultures as well as portraying processes that take place in the borderlands. We wanted to build solidarity among people living on both sides of the EU border that for centuries were interconnected in language and culture. We tried to check how much the border was impeding free intercultural exchange nowadays. We especially checked how strong influences from abroad were in everyday life: in music, dressing style and using social media.

During our activities we analyzed traditional dances and music of both regions, mutual influences between our cultures and factors that shaped them. The idea behind MAPS came from a growing need to rethink the old concepts that do not fit our reality anymore, from wishing to change perspectives and to mock prejudice by tackling critical thinking. It was a call to recognize and escape different identity traps, get rid of artificial borders which limit our personalities, and understand better who we are, and how we are “made and remade continually”, as Virginia Woolf once said.

 Shakespeare's 'Romeo and Juliet' was selected as the theme of the drama workshops, as the resounding themes of passion, love, betrayal, rejection and redemption are powerful images for young people to explore. Love in Romeo and Juliet is a brutal, powerful emotion that captures individuals and catapults them against their world, and, at times, against themselves. A series of workshops over seven days will explore the relationship of the human to nature and to each other, and culminate in a performance. The themes of cultural strangeness in the play will be echoed in the cultural differences between the participants; only the death of lovers brings everyone to their senses so their families and friends can live and work together peacefully. Shakespearean drama is full of powerful archetypes and characters that create opportunities to explore many aspects of humanity. projects.title_en: YE - Circular Economy in European Supply Chains
projects.objective: With the European Commission’s actions through the circular economy package and the CE stakeholder forum as a backdrop, we are seeking to map current developments and new initiatives in the European private sector with a focus on the Netherlands. This project brings together 17 young people (age 18 to 28) – supervised by one Norwegian and one Dutch youth NGO – which will work together over the course of 4,5 months towards one practical goal: to visit and learn from key actors – corporate and academic – that exhibit best-practice initiatives that help reduce unnecessary spillage and increase recycling rates. Our final goal is to synthesise our findings into a constructive policy report which will educate our member-bases as well as provide prescriptions on the topic of circular economy to domestic and European stakeholders. To enable this, we will spend 6 days in The Hague in November 2018, engaging in workshops and visits and getting to grips with two key questions: Firstly, how European (national as well as EU) policies are facilitating (or hampering) the push towards the circular economy; secondly, how European firms work together across their value chains to achieve their goals

The project was held in Loisy, France. It united young people from 5 countries at the youth exchange on the topic of healthy lifestyle and sport. Everyone knows the obvious behaviors that describe someone, who is healthy and takes care of themselves. A healthy person doesn't smoke, tries to maintain a healthy weight, eats healthy foods with plenty of fruits, vegetables and fiber and, of course, exercises on a regular basis, knows how to manage stress, gets good quality sleep each night, doesn't drink too much, doesn't sit too much—basically, does everything in moderation all the time. projects.title_en: Gaming Old School Style
projects.objective:
The project entitled “Gaming Old School Style” was a youth exchange addressed at young people interested in board games and role-playing games (RPG). The main activity took place in Poland, with 30 participants from 6 countries meeting in the village of Nowy Gierałtów. The idea for the project was born during conversations among a group of young people who wish to share their interest in “old school gaming”. Participants wanted to popularize this particular hobby and show how beneficial board and role-playing games can be for personal development. The exchange lasted 6 days (plus travel), with each day devoted to a different set of adventure and strategy games, as well as card games. The participants had a wider selection of games than the time available to try all of them out. Among the titles we can name the following: Journeys through Middle Earth, New Angeles, Dixit, Betrayal at the House on the Hill, Mansions of Madness, Elder Sign, Eldritch Horror, Warewolf, Pathfinder, Lancaster, Warhammer: Underworlds, Story Cubes, Avalon, Talisman, Saboteur, Mafia and Jenga.

projects.objective: The Get Green get better, project was carried out in Slovenia, in Veržej. The project was carried out in order to spend more time in nature for young people, to spend quality free time, to engage in sports activities, to be more eco-conscious and to learn as many ways as possible to reuse waste. The project was designed to make it easier for young people to have a stress-free life. With this project, we reconnected them with nature, and became more aware of the importance of recycling and saving. Youth exchanges were attended by three young people from Croatia, five from Jordan, Egypt and Portugal and thirteen from Slovenia. Eighteen women and thirteen men took part in the project. They care for the preservation of cultural landscapes in Germany to benefit nature conservation as well as a good living for the regional population. Often they act as mediators between different stakeholders, mostley in rural areas. The return of the wolf to Germany has created many conflicts, both in the regions where packs are resident, and in regions known as wolf awaiting lands. How to deal with the wolf is often not clear. However, strategies and solutions are needed to solve the conflict and pass on sientific and non emotional information. This is where Landcare Associations and Landcare Germany start, as they inform stakeholders and interested parties about the current situation in the region, discuss fears and challenges, and seek solutions together in various public events and trainings. The goal of the applied project is to disminish or solve conflicts caused by the wolves by trainings for adults offered by Landcare Associations. The use of electronic devices on vehicles is increasing and the amount of information that the diagnostic system can provide is extensive and varies, opening new opportunities for the repair world. The "connected vehicle" of the future will be recorded and send the driving data, the information on its state of operation and the stresses that are subject to its various components.
